To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
resveratrol improves diastolic function and energy metabolism in mice with pressure-overload HF.
resveratrol improves diastolic function and cardiac energy metabolism in a murine model of pressure-overload– induced heart failure.

resveratrol administration to mice with established pressure-overload– induced heart failure (HF), despite a lack of improvement of ejection fraction, lessens the severity and duration of the HF phenotype, improves diastolic function of the heart, restores mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, improves cardiac energy metabolism, lessens cardiac fibrosis, and improves peripheral insulin sensitivity, vasodilator function, and physical function of the animals.

the use of a natural product to treat and manage established heart failure, a condition that affects millions worldwide and for which no cure currently exists.
the development of new therapeutic approaches for the treatment of HF, which is a major cause of mortality and morbidity in the developed world.
the development of a new treatment for HF.

resveratrol is a potential treatment for patients with established HF.

resveratrol is a potential therapeutic for the treatment and/or management of HF.
